title: The Italian Salumeria Board
h1: Italian Salumeria Board: A $250 Luxury Charcuterie Board
seo_title: Luxury Italian Charcuterie Board: $250 Salumeria Board for 10
description: A $250 luxury Italian charcuterie board for 10: 30-month Parmigiano Reggiano, 24-month Prosciutto di Parma, bresaola, mortadella, finocchiona, burrata and traditional aged balsamic.
hook: At $250 the board is built on Italy's protected classics: 30-month Parmigiano Reggiano, hand-sliced Prosciutto di Parma and a traditional aged balsamic poured a few drops at a time, with fresh burrata torn open at the table.

items.name: Traditional balsamic vinegar of Modena, aged, 100 ml

why: Breaking long-aged Parmigiano along its grain shows the crunchy crystals that only come with age, and a few drops of thick, traditional balsamic on each chunk is a classic pairing from Emilia-Romagna. That one bottle is a third of the budget, and it is the bite guests remember.

Four cured meats in four shapes let guests tell them apart: translucent prosciutto in loose folds, lean bresaola in a circle, silky mortadella in quarters and fennel-scented finocchiona in a shingled row. Torn burrata becomes the board's dip, and sweet figs and buttery green olives balance all that salt.

timeline.what: Take out the Parmigiano and gorgonzola.
Break the Parmigiano into craggy chunks.
Separate the prosciutto slices; fold the mortadella.
Halve the figs; drain the olives.
Tear the burrata at the table.

faq.q: What makes an Italian charcuterie board luxury?
faq.a: The protected, long-aged foods: Parmigiano Reggiano aged 30 months, Prosciutto di Parma aged 24 months and hand-sliced, and traditional balsamic vinegar of Modena, which is aged for years and used a few drops at a time.

faq.q: How much does a luxury Italian charcuterie board cost?
faq.a: This one comes to about $232 for 10 at Whole Foods plus an online order for the balsamic, at regular fall 2026 prices. Swapping the traditional balsamic for an aged IGP bottle saves about $76.

faq.q: Where do you buy traditional balsamic vinegar?
faq.a: Specialty Italian importers and some cheese shops carry it in 100 ml bottles. Look for the words traditional and DOP on the label; the cheaper IGP bottles are a different, younger product.
